text: Burlington Signs National (the "Applicant") made a variance application concerning one first party illuminated wall sign displaying static copy (the "Proposed Sign"), to be located on portions of the ninth and tenth storeys of the southerly elevation of a hotel building located at 970 Dixon Road (the "Premises"). After conducting a written hearing in accordance with the requirements of the Sign By-law, a decision was made to refuse to grant the necessary variances. Ruth's Chris Steak House (the "Appellant") subsequently filed an appeal of the decision. Staff have determined that there was not enough information provided in the application to establish that the Proposed Sign meets all nine of the established criteria as contained in §694-30A of the Sign By-law. Granted the following variances for the Proposed Sign as described in Attachment 1 of the report (January 9, 2018) from the Manager, Sign By-law Unit, Toronto Building proposed to be located within the premises municipally known as 970 Dixon Road: a. The requirement contained at §694-21I(4)(a) which states that in an E-Employment sign district, a wall sign displaying the logo or corporate symbol of a business located on the premises is permitted provided the sign is erected on an office building containing 10 or more storeys, be varied to allow for the Proposed Sign displaying the logo or corporate symbol of a business located on the premises is to be erected on a thirteen storey building which is not an office building. b.
